topics.why_in_news: Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill 2026 was introduced in Lok Sabha to decriminalise minor offences and improve Ease of Doing Business and governance efficiency.
prelims_quick_notes: Proposes decriminalisation of 717 provisions.
Amends 784 provisions across 79 Central Acts.
Covers laws under 23 Ministries.
Focuses on Ease of Doing Business and Ease of Living.
Replaces imprisonment for minor procedural violations with monetary penalties or warnings.
Introduces graded penalties system.
Provides adjudicating officers and appellate authorities.
Builds on Jan Vishwas Act 2023.
important_facts: Introduced by Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
One of India's largest regulatory rationalisation exercises.
Aims to reduce compliance burden and inspector raj.
Supports trust-based governance model.
Select Committee recommended expansion across additional Central Acts.
exam_relevance: Important for governance reforms and Ease of Doing Business.
Useful for Polity, Governance and Economy sections.
Can be linked to Article 21, administrative reforms and regulatory governance.
prelims_traps: Bill does not remove penalties completely.
Focus is mainly on minor procedural and technical defaults.

topics.topic: Subhash Chandra Bose Aapda Prabandhan Puraskar
topics.why_in_news: PIB announced that nominations for Subhash Chandra Bose Aapda Prabandhan Puraskar are open throughout the year through the National Awards Portal to strengthen disaster resilience and participation.
prelims_quick_notes: Instituted in 2019 by Ministry of Home Affairs.
Announced annually on 23 January (Parakram Diwas).
Recognises excellence in disaster management.
Open to individuals and institutions.
Covers prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, relief, rehabilitation and reconstruction.
Supports innovation, community awareness and capacity building.
Linked with Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction.
Nominations accepted through National Awards Portal.
important_facts: Cash award: ₹5 lakh for individuals.
Cash award: ₹51 lakh for institutions.
Disaster Management Act 2005 institutionalised NDMA, SDMAs and DDMAs.
India achieved major reduction in cyclone-related mortality after Odisha Super Cyclone 1999.
Award acts as a soft governance instrument for disaster management.
exam_relevance: Important for Disaster Management and Governance.
Useful for NDMA, cooperative federalism and resilience-building topics.
Can be linked with Sendai Framework and climate-induced disasters.
prelims_traps: Award was instituted in 2019, not under Disaster Management Act 2005.
Announced on Parakram Diwas, not National Disaster Management Day.
Covers full disaster management cycle, not only disaster response.

topics.why_in_news: Bharat Electricity Summit 2026 highlighted India’s transition towards clean energy, energy security and expansion of power infrastructure to meet growing electricity demand.
prelims_quick_notes: Focused on India’s long-term power sector transformation.
Emphasised renewable energy expansion and green transition.
Discussed energy security and electricity accessibility.
Highlighted importance of transmission infrastructure.
Promoted smart grids and energy efficiency measures.
Focused on reducing dependence on fossil fuels.
Supported India's net-zero commitments.
Encouraged public-private participation in power sector.
important_facts: India targets 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.
Renewable energy includes solar, wind, hydro and biomass.
Power sector is crucial for industrial growth and digital economy.
Green Hydrogen Mission linked with future energy transition.
Electricity demand in India expected to rise significantly with urbanisation and industrialisation.
exam_relevance: Important for Economy, Environment and Infrastructure topics.
Useful for renewable energy, climate commitments and sustainable development.
Can be linked with COP commitments and energy transition.
prelims_traps: Renewable energy and non-fossil fuel energy are not exactly the same.
Hydropower is classified under renewable energy.
Net-zero target refers to balancing emissions, not zero emissions immediately.

topics.why_in_news: PIB highlighted India's achievements in vaccination coverage and strengthening of the Universal Immunisation Programme through Mission Indradhanush and digital health initiatives.
prelims_quick_notes: Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) launched in 1985.
One of the world’s largest public health programmes.
Implemented by Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Provides free vaccination against major vaccine-preventable diseases.
Targets pregnant women, infants and children.
Mission Indradhanush launched to improve immunisation coverage.
Intensified Mission Indradhanush focuses on low-coverage districts.
Digital platforms like U-WIN support vaccination tracking.
important_facts: UIP covers diseases such as tuberculosis, polio, diphtheria, tetanus, measles and hepatitis B.
Pulse Polio Programme helped India become polio-free in 2014.
WHO certification recognised India as polio-free region.
Vaccination contributes to reduction in infant and maternal mortality.
Cold chain infrastructure is critical for vaccine storage and transport.
exam_relevance: Important for Health, Social Justice and Governance.
Useful for questions on public health infrastructure and SDGs.
Can be linked with child welfare and preventive healthcare.
prelims_traps: UIP is a Central government programme implemented with state participation.
Mission Indradhanush is not separate from UIP.
Polio-free status does not mean vaccination programmes have stopped.

topics.why_in_news: Department of Posts launched ‘24 Speed Post’ service providing next-day guaranteed delivery to improve logistics efficiency and premium postal services in India.
prelims_quick_notes: Launched by Department of Posts in March 2026.
Provides D+1 guaranteed delivery service.
Initially launched across major metro cities.
Aims to improve speed and reliability of postal delivery.
Includes end-to-end tracking and SMS alerts.
Supports e-commerce and business logistics.
Offers OTP-based secure delivery.
Includes money-back guarantee for service failure.
important_facts: Postal services fall under Union List.
India Post is one of the world’s largest postal networks.
Supports Digital India and logistics modernisation.
Useful for MSMEs, e-commerce and document delivery.
Linked with infrastructure and logistics reforms.
exam_relevance: Important for Governance, Infrastructure and Economy.
Useful for logistics, public service delivery and Digital India topics.
Can be linked with National Logistics Policy and e-commerce growth.
prelims_traps: D+1 means next-day delivery from booking date.
24 Speed Post is not a private courier service.
Postal services come under Union List, not State List.
